html:
A Japanese writer, teacher and publisher who did more than anyone to explain the West to the Japanese public in the years of the Meiji Restoration. He founded what became Keio University.

The son of a low-ranking samurai, he studied Dutch learning in Osaka. When he visited the new port of Yokohama in 1859 he found that foreigners spoke English, not Dutch, so he taught himself English. He sailed with Japan's first mission to the United States in 1860.

His book Conditions in the West described Western schools, banks, hospitals and governments, and sold in huge numbers. In An Encouragement of Learning he wrote that "Heaven does not create one person above or below another", urging independence and practical study over old Confucian learning.

He ran a school from 1858, renamed Keio Gijuku in 1868, and founded a newspaper. In later years he urged Japan to turn away from China and Korea and follow the West. His face was on the 10,000 yen note from 1984 to 2024.
sum: A Japanese writer, teacher and publisher who did more than anyone to explain the West to the Japanese public in the years of the Meiji Restoration. He founded what became Keio University.
